title: Compactness verifies the rational derived Hom comparison
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. Module sheaves, sheaf tensor products, derived categories and cohomology are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,A)$ for the completed integral category including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and $Q:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=\mathcal C_X[1/\varpi]$ for its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. A rational module sheaf is constructible when on a finite locally closed stratification it is pro-etale locally finite free [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Write $F_X(K)=E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$ and $J_X(QK)=F_X(K)$, $J_X(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)$ for the functor specified in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. For $K\in\mathcal C_X$ and every countable family $(M_i)$ in $D(B_X)$ with a common cohomological lower bound, the canonical map $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(K,M_i[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,(\bigoplus_iM_i)[q])$ is an isomorphism for every integer $q$. In particular, for $K,L\in\mathcal C_X$ the actual scalar-extension map gives natural isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B_X)}(K,L[q])[1/\varpi]\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(E_X)}(F_XK,F_XL[q]),\qquad f/\varpi^n\longmapsto\varpi^{-n}F_X(f).$$
They commute with shifts, identities and composition. Thus $J_X$ is fully faithful into the actual ambient $D(E_X)$. The first assertion verifies, rather than assumes, the coproduct-Hom hypothesis in [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-derived-hom], using the global-derived-Hom continuity of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-bounded-below-compactness].

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), full faithfulness, pp. 61-62

proof.text: Use the canonical coefficient identification in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]: the completed sheaf $B_X$ is the continuous-function sheaf $A_X$. Thus $K$ belongs to the same full integral category under this identification. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-hom-sums] with this $X,E,A,\varpi,K$ and the given countable family. The scheme is noetherian and finite-dimensional, $\ell$ is invertible, and the family has the common lower bound required there. Its conclusion is exactly the first displayed map for every $q\in\mathbf Z$, with the same shifted coprojections, so proves the first assertion. This existing Hom-sums theorem is the passage from the global-derived-Hom continuity of Lemma 6.8.12 to ordinary shifted Hom; no continuity for families unbounded below is invoked.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), full faithfulness, pp. 61-62

proof.text: Apply (i)$\Rightarrow$(iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] to $L\in\mathcal C_X$. All its scheme and coefficient hypotheses are those of the item, and membership includes the compatible etale-origin witnesses. It follows that $L$ is bounded, hence bounded below. The same characterization states closure under shifts, so $L[q]$ is again in $\mathcal C_X$ whenever needed to interpret a morphism of the rational category. No projectivity or flatness of the cohomology modules of $L$ is being assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), full faithfulness, pp. 61-62

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-derived-hom] on the small site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the commutative ring $A$, scalar $t=\varpi$, ring sheaf $R=B_X$ and $R_t=E_X$. Step 1 verifies precisely its countable, common-lower-bound coproduct-Hom hypothesis on $K$ for every integer shift; Step 2 verifies its bounded-below hypothesis on $L$. By [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor], scalar localization is exact on module sheaves and its induced triangulated functor is the actual $F_X=E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}-$ used in the item. The theorem therefore gives the natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B_X)}(K,L[q])[1/\varpi]\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(E_X)}(F_XK,F_XL[q])$, with the specified image $f/\varpi^n\mapsto\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)$. In particular it is the actual scalar-extension comparison, with its shift comparison, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of the two modules.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), full faithfulness, pp. 61-62

proof.text: For completeness, the fraction formula gives precomposition and postcomposition by $a,b$ as $\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)F_X(a)$ and $F_X(b)\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)$, so gives naturality. Shifting gives $\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)[r]$ under the triangulated shift identification. The identity fraction maps to $F_X(1)=1$, and for composable fractions the formula gives $\varpi^{-(m+n)}F_X(gf)=(\varpi^{-m}F_X(g))(\varpi^{-n}F_X(f))$. These equations hold for every fraction. Finally [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] defines $\mathcal C_X$ as a full subcategory of $D(B_X)$, and [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] gives every object of $\mathcal R_X$ as $QK$ and its Hom modules as the localized integral Hom modules. The $q=0$ bijections of Step 3 are therefore exactly the Hom maps of $J_X$ specified in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. They prove that $J_X$ is fully faithful into the ambient $D(E_X)$.

The proof expands exactly that implication. The delivery is one commit with no new nodes; statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are byte-identical to the unsplit live node; there is no cycle (closure of 2722 nodes); and the item is not superseded, has no repair note and is not on the drop list. Step 1: lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-hom-sums states the first assertion verbatim (same E, A, ϖ, noetherian finite-dimensional X with ℓ invertible, K in the complete category, small countable families with a common lower bound, every q, shifted coprojections). The coefficient identification B_X=C(|−|,A) comes from the realization-functor node through the same continuous-coefficients node. Step 2: (i)⇒(iii) of the integral stratified-perfect characterization gives L bounded, and the same node gives closure under shifts. Step 3: I checked every hypothesis of the scalar-localization theorem: small site, t=ϖ, R=B_X, R_t=E_X as the sheafified section localization, the K-hypothesis at every q from Step 1, L bounded below from Step 2, and F equal to the actual scalar localization by the realization-functor node. Its conclusion is the item's display, with naturality, shifts and composition. Step 4 is elementary: the complete category is a full subcategory of D(B_X), and the rational category has the same objects with Hom⊗E and no Karoubi envelope, so the q=0 maps are those of J_X and J_X is fully faithful. Edge cases are consistent: empty family, K=0 or L=0, negative q, and ϖ-torsion K (both sides 0). Neither the cited nodes nor the item claim anything for families unbounded below. I accept the tool_uses of the three generic pbc nodes; the parent already carries two of them. lean.note: The first conjunct verifies the actual shifted-coprojection map for every small countable family, including the empty family.
